title: The spectral theorem and the Dirichlet problem
summary: The spectrum of self-adjoint operators; eigenspaces of compact self-adjoint operators; the spectral theorem; application to the Dirichlet problem on an interval.

objectives.description: State the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem including the kernel and range closure.
Derive and check the Dirichlet Green operator, its eigenvalues and a norm error estimate.
Use spectral positivity to solve a variable-potential boundary problem and diagnose resonance when positivity is lost.

preparation.description: Read Lectures 21–23 of the 18.102 Spring 2021 notes.

activities.instructions: Write the complete proof portfolio with the named hypotheses visible. Start independently, use hints progressively, and retain any corrections made after source reading or feedback. Revisit the central argument without notes after a gap.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The compact spectral theorem says the range is closed.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The eigenvectors span its closure. A compact injective diagonal with eigenvalues tending to zero has a dense nonclosed range.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A Fourier series solution can always be differentiated term by term.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The convergence mode and derivative estimates must justify that step. Here the integral equation supplies classical regularity instead.
